results.evidence: No outside source states a car-to-car gain for the Fricaba scramble via Home Lake/Constance Pass. Published figures are for the Home Lake hike alone (about 6,000 ft round trip on one hiking page, about 4,800 ft on a trail-map page), which do not include the summit day. Per the rules gain_ft is not recomputed from arithmetic; the 4,259 vs 5,600 split stays open.

results.correct_value: 9.3 mi one way (Upper Dungeness TH to Home Lake)
results.evidence: A trail-guide page puts Home Lake at 9.3 mi from the Upper Dungeness trailhead (Camp Handy 3.4, Boulder Shelter 6.1). A hiking page gives 19.4 mi round trip (about 9.7 one way) and a trail-map page 19.6 mi round trip. All sources put Home Lake well beyond 9 miles; the itinerary's 7.9 is the outlier. Adopted 9.3 to match the waypoint and approach text; day 1 and day 3 miles and the total note updated (7 mi summit day left as is).

results.fact: Is Home Lake inside the national park (permit needed?)
results.correct_value: Home Lake is inside Olympic National Park; a park wilderness permit is needed to camp there. Camp Handy and Boulder Shelter are national forest (no permit).
results.evidence: The Forest Service page for Home Lake Trail #893 says it runs 0.9 mi from Boulder Shelter to the park boundary, where it becomes the Constance Pass Trail leading to Home Lake within Olympic National Park. A hiking guide states Home Lake is in Olympic National Park and a permit must be reserved; a regional travel article also places the park entry before Home Lake. overnight_permit.where was the outlier.

patches.fact: Is Home Lake inside the national park (permit needed?)
patches.find: Camp Handy, Boulder Shelter and Home Lake are on national forest land; a recreation pass is needed to park. A park wilderness permit is needed only to camp across Constance Pass.
patches.replace: Camp Handy and Boulder Shelter are on national forest land; a recreation pass is needed to park. A park wilderness permit is needed to camp at Home Lake or anywhere past the park boundary, about a mile beyond Boulder Shelter.

results.evidence: Sources confirm Deception Basin can be reached off-trail from the Constance Pass side, but the standard approach described for Mystery and Deception is from Royal Basin; no two sources name Home Lake as the standard base camp for Deception/Mystery. The bivy sentence is part of the regional camp list owned by the camping clean-up, so no patch either way.

results.correct_value: No permit is needed in the Buckhorn Wilderness; a reserved park wilderness permit is needed to camp inside Olympic National Park (including Home Lake).
results.evidence: The Olympic National Forest wilderness page says no permit is needed to visit Olympic National Forest wilderness areas; permits apply only inside the national park. A trip guide for the Upper Dungeness likewise says no permit is needed to camp in the Buckhorn Wilderness but a park permit is needed for Home Lake. The partner-requirements line claiming a self-issued Buckhorn permit is the outlier.

patches.find: self-issued Buckhorn Wilderness permit, backcountry permit if camping inside Olympic National Park
patches.replace: none needed in the Buckhorn Wilderness; a reserved wilderness permit to camp inside Olympic National Park, including Home Lake

results.evidence: No source gives the Home Lake–Constance Pass–Deception Basin–Fricaba round-trip distance. Home Lake is 0.5 mi below Constance Pass; the rest of the line is off-trail with no published mileage. The waypoint distMi values (9.3 to 11.3) are themselves unsourced, so neither the 7 mi day nor the 4 mi implied by the pins can be confirmed.

results.evidence: partner_requirements.fitnessSpec.hiking says an 18-21 mile round trip, but the Home Lake hike alone is about 18.6-19.6 mi round trip per published trail figures, before any summit day, and the itinerary totals 25.6 mi after the day-1/day-3 fix.
